angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 7,570,344 km at 121.67 pc = 0.83 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 8.2192 +/- 0.0166 mas (same row, RUWE 1.02): 121.67 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 10.882 (10.663 to 11.100) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 7,570,344 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.361 (1.280 to 1.401) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4574 +/- 0.8 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 497653157602636928: teff_gspphot 4574.2593 K (16th-84th percentiles 4573.531-4575.221), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 497653157602636928: teff_gspphot 4574.2593 K (16th-84th percentiles 4573.531-4575.221), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/mago.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 2.499, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
